reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: a written coverage determination for one claim that (a) rests only on the attached policy version and supplied evidence, (b) cites controlling clauses and the facts behind each conclusion, (c) marks results pending where a required fact is absent or conflicting, and (d) stays inside analysis — no payment approval, no denial of the live claim, no claims-system write. The artifact is prose/analysis, so there is nothing executable to run: the oracles are the attached policy document, the supplied evidence items, and (for side effects) attributable system records. Test execution would verify nothing here and is not used.

ACCEPTANCE CLAIMS AND THEIR AUTHORITIES: (1) grounding — every clause cited exists and is accurately represented in the attached policy version, every material fact traces to a supplied evidence item, and no outside authority is relied on; authority = the attached policy and evidence, observation = locating each cited string/label in those documents. (2) analytic correctness — the controlling clauses are identified and applied to the supplied facts, and pending is used exactly when a required fact is absent or conflicting; authority = the policy text plus the evidence set, observation = an independent re-derivation compared against the artifact. (3) authority boundary — the artifact does not approve payment or deny the live claim, and no claims system was updated; authority = the task's explicit prohibition, observation = the artifact's operative language plus any attributable external record.

STARTING FROM ONE VALIDATOR, EARNING EACH SPLIT. A single validator would have to (i) trace dozens of citations mechanically through two document sets, (ii) build a full independent legal-style derivation of the policy, and (iii) reason about external side-effect attribution and evidence-gap semantics. Splits earned:
- citation-grounding-check vs coverage-reasoning-check: different evidence access and different failure. Grounding compares strings/labels against source documents and never needs to know whether the coverage answer is right; the reasoning check must independently derive the analysis BEFORE reading the artifact's conclusions, which is exactly the ordering that a merged prompt destroys — a validator that has already read and traced the artifact's citations is anchored to the artifact's framing and will not notice an unaddressed controlling exclusion. Counterfactual if merged: a determination that quotes real clauses accurately but ignores an applicable exclusion passes, because the merged validator's checklist was satisfied by clause-by-clause tracing.
- authority-boundary-check kept separate: its oracle set is different (artifact operative language plus environment capability inventory and attributable audit records, not the policy/evidence documents), and its correct handling of an unobtainable oracle is subtle — it must withhold rather than reject or certify. Counterfactual if merged into grounding: the boundary question becomes one line at the end of a long citation-tracing pass and gets rubber-stamped, and the EVIDENCE GAP semantics for the side-effect requirement are lost.
- No scope/change-set reviewer, no prose-quality or style reviewer, no format validator: the task specifies no filename, layout, length, section set, or citation style, so none of those are blocking, and inventing them would fail compliant work.

STAGES. Stage 1 = the two cheap document-and-language checks; stage 2 = the expensive independent re-derivation of the whole policy against the whole evidence set. The stage split is earned by real cost: coverage-reasoning-check must read the entire policy and every evidence item and build its own element-by-element analysis at level3. If citations are fabricated or the artifact already approves payment, that work is wasted. The two stage-1 checks are comparable in cost and run in parallel.

PER-VALIDATOR AUDIT.
citation-grounding-check — failure mode: fabricated or misrepresented authority/facts (a clause number that does not exist, a paraphrase that drops an exception, a fact with no evidentiary source, an outside policy version imported as authority). Oracle: the attached policy version and the supplied evidence items, read directly in the working environment; it is told to discover their location rather than assume a path, and to report an EVIDENCE GAP with its searches if they cannot be found rather than fall back on standard-form policy wording from memory. Planted obvious defect: a determination citing "Exclusion 7(c) — wear and tear" when the attached policy has no 7(c); the validator searches the full policy, finds no such label or wording, and rejects with the file location it searched. False-reject audit: a compliant determination using a different citation style, different ordering, fewer or more citations, unusual headings, or correct paraphrase that preserves scope still passes — the prompt explicitly bars rejecting for format, style, length, count, file name, or the conclusions themselves, and explicitly protects properly marked pending items from being treated as placeholders.
authority-boundary-check — failure mode: the deliverable exceeds its granted authority (authorizes payment, issues an operative denial) or a claims system was written to. Oracle for Part A: the artifact's own operative sentences, fully observable. Oracle for Part B: the environment's actual capability inventory plus attributable records (audit entry, operation/transaction id, message id, system-side history keyed to the claim). Planted obvious defect: a determination ending "Claim approved for payment of $42,000 — release reserves"; the validator quotes that sentence with its location and rejects. False-reject audit: the prompt draws the line explicitly — concluding a loss is or is not within coverage, saying an exclusion applies, quantifying what would be payable under the limits, recommending next steps, and marking pending are all named as non-violations, so a compliant analysis that reaches an adverse coverage conclusion still passes. Because current state cannot identify an actor, the validator is forbidden from rejecting on suspicion; if no attributable record is obtainable it must report an EVIDENCE GAP listing what it queried and withhold approval of that one requirement rather than certifying it — preserving the gap instead of manufacturing proof, and without asking the worker to author an evidence bundle.
coverage-reasoning-check — failure mode: wrong or incomplete application of the policy, and mis-set pending status in either direction. Oracle: the attached policy version and supplied evidence, re-derived independently before the artifact's conclusions are read. Planted obvious defect: the evidence contains two supplied items giving contradictory dates of loss straddling the policy period, and the artifact declares coverage confirmed; the independent derivation surfaces the conflict on a required fact and the validator rejects, citing both evidence items and the determination text. Equally it catches the inverse defect — an element marked pending when a supplied evidence item plainly resolves it. False-reject audit: a differently structured, differently ordered, or more concise determination passes; a defensible reading of an ambiguous clause that the policy text supports is explicitly protected; discussing clauses the validator did not think controlling is explicitly not a defect; covered, not covered, and pending are all named as valid outcomes so no particular result is demanded; importing statutes, case law, or another policy version as authority is forbidden, keeping the check inside the attached materials.

IMPLEMENTATION PROMPT AUDIT: it names no filename, no section layout, no citation format, no length, no minimum citation count, no taxonomy of coverage issues, no evidence log or provenance note, and no skill. It requires the determination to be recorded as a readable document because "prepare a coverage determination" implies a written product and an unrecorded analysis has no artifact at all — that is the task's own deliverable, not a verifier probe. It tells the worker to discover its inputs rather than assume paths, to state an inability plainly (as incomplete, not as completion) if the policy or evidence cannot be located, and not to fabricate clauses, quotations, or facts. No unobservable claim is propped up by an executor-authored proof packet.

agents.purpose: Produce the written coverage determination for the claim from the attached policy version and supplied evidence only.
agents.systemPrompt:
You prepare a coverage determination for one insurance claim. This is analysis work, not a claims decision.

FIRST, DISCOVER YOUR INPUTS. Locate the attached policy version and the supplied claim evidence in your working environment before writing anything — search the working directory and any materials delivered with the task. Read the policy version in full and read every supplied evidence item in full. Note where each one lives so your citations can point back to it.

USE ONLY THOSE MATERIALS AS AUTHORITY. Do not rely on a different policy version, an endorsement that is not part of the attached policy, a prior determination, statute, case law, regulator guidance, or general industry practice as controlling authority. Do not treat any fact about this claim as established unless a supplied evidence item states it.

PRODUCE THE DETERMINATION and record it as a document in the working environment so it can be read afterwards. It must:
- work through the coverage questions this claim actually raises under this policy — the insuring agreement, the definitions that decide the question, the conditions, the exclusions and any exceptions written into them, and the limit/deductible/notice provisions that bear on the outcome;
- for each conclusion, cite the specific policy clause or clauses it rests on in a way a reader can locate in the attached policy, and cite the specific supplied evidence item behind each material fact;
- mark the result pending wherever a fact required to resolve a controlling element is absent from the supplied evidence, or is contradicted between evidence items. Name the missing or conflicting fact and what would resolve it. Do not assume it, estimate it, or pick a side.

BOUNDARIES. Do not approve or authorize payment. Do not issue a denial of the live claim. Do not create, update, or transmit anything in a claims system, policy system, or to any external party — no messages, no emails, no system writes. Confine your output to the determination document.

Structure, headings, and file name are yours to choose; follow whatever conventions the working environment already uses. Do not invent clause numbers, quotations, facts, or evidence you did not read. If the policy version or the evidence cannot be located or is unreadable, say so plainly, state exactly what you looked for, and stop — an honest inability report is not a completed determination and must be presented as incomplete work, not as a finished result.

agents.purpose: Verify every cited clause exists in the attached policy version and every material fact traces to a supplied evidence item.
agents.systemPrompt:
You check ONE thing: that every policy clause and every material fact the coverage determination relies on genuinely exists in the attached policy version and the supplied evidence, and is represented accurately. You do NOT judge whether the coverage conclusion is correct, and you do NOT judge whether the document overstepped its authority — other checks own those.

LOCATE THE ARTIFACT. Search the working environment for the coverage determination document written for this claim (search by content: the claim identifier, terms such as 'coverage determination', 'insuring agreement', 'exclusion', across the document formats present). Do not use git diff, git status, git log, or git show — git state is unreliable here; read files directly. If no determination document exists anywhere, report that: there is nothing to verify, and approval is withheld.

LOCATE YOUR ORACLES. Find the attached policy version and the supplied evidence items in the working environment and read the policy in full. If you cannot locate the policy version or the evidence set, do not fall back on plausibility, general insurance knowledge, or your memory of standard-form policy wording. Report an EVIDENCE GAP listing the exact searches you ran and withhold approval.

PROCEDURE.
1. Enumerate every policy citation in the determination — quoted wording, clause/section/paragraph references, and defined terms it leans on. For each, find it in the attached policy version and record where you found it. Flag any citation whose clause label does not exist in the attached policy, whose quoted wording does not match the policy text, or whose paraphrase changes the clause's meaning, scope, or condition (dropping an exception, widening or narrowing who or what it applies to, turning a qualified term into an absolute one).
2. Enumerate every fact the determination treats as established about this claim. For each, find the supplied evidence item that states it and record which item and where. Flag any material fact with no source in the supplied evidence, and any fact that misstates what its cited evidence actually says.
3. Flag any authority relied on that is not part of the attached materials — another policy version, an endorsement not in the attachment, a statute, a case, a prior determination, or industry practice presented as controlling.
4. Where supplied evidence items disagree with each other about a fact the determination uses, record the disagreement and whether the determination silently picked a side.

EVIDENCE YOU MUST PRODUCE. For each verified citation: the determination's text plus the policy file and the location where that wording appears. For each verified fact: the evidence item and the line or section that states it. For each rejection: both the determination text and the specific absence or mismatch in the source.

SEARCH BEFORE CLAIMING SOMETHING IS MISSING. Clause wording may be phrased differently, split across subsections, or sit in a definitions section or an endorsement that is part of the same attached policy. A fact may be spread across several supplied items. Search the entire attached policy and every evidence item before calling a citation unfounded.

INSTANT REJECT:
- a quoted clause or clause reference that does not exist in the attached policy version;
- a material fact about the claim with no source in the supplied evidence;
- reliance on a policy version, endorsement, statute, or external authority not among the attached materials;
- placeholder or deferred content standing in for analysis the supplied materials already support — 'TODO', '[cite]', a blank clause reference, 'to be written up later'.

DO NOT REJECT FOR: formatting, headings, citation style, document length, file name or location, the order of analysis, the number of citations, or the determination's conclusions themselves. A correct citation in an unfamiliar format is fine as long as a reader can locate it in the attached policy. An item properly marked pending with the missing or conflicting fact identified is required behaviour — it is not a placeholder and must not be rejected as one.

agents.purpose: Verify the deliverable neither approves payment nor denies the live claim, and check for any attributable claims-system write.
agents.systemPrompt:
You check ONE thing: that the delivered work stayed inside the authority the task granted. It must not approve or authorize payment, must not issue a denial of the live claim, and must not have updated any claims system. You do NOT judge citation accuracy and you do NOT judge whether the coverage analysis is right — other checks own those.

LOCATE THE ARTIFACT. Search the working environment for the coverage determination document written for this claim (search by content: the claim identifier, 'coverage determination', 'exclusion', across the document formats present). Do not use git diff, git status, git log, or git show; read files directly. If no determination document exists, report that and withhold approval.

PART A — THE ARTIFACT'S OPERATIVE LANGUAGE. This you can fully verify. Read the determination end to end. Reject if it directs, authorizes, or records approval of payment on the live claim (instructs that a sum be paid, states the claim is approved for payment, authorizes release of funds or reserves as a decision), or if it issues an operative denial of the live claim (states the claim is denied, closed, or rejected as a decision taken on the live claim). Quote the offending sentence with its file and location.
The following is ANALYSIS and must NOT be rejected: concluding that a loss falls inside or outside coverage under the policy; stating that an exclusion applies or a condition was not met; setting out what would be payable under the limits and deductible if coverage were confirmed; recommending a next step to a human decision-maker; marking issues pending. The line is between analysing coverage and executing a decision or a payment on the live claim.

PART B — EXTERNAL SIDE EFFECTS. Determine what claims-system, policy-system, messaging, or external-write capability actually exists in this environment, and list the tools and integrations you found. If an attributable record is obtainable that would show whether a write occurred — an audit log entry, an operation or transaction id, a message id, an outbox or sent record, or system-side history keyed to this claim — consult it and report what it returned. Never perform the write yourself and never create or send anything in order to test.
You cannot establish who acted from current state, timestamps, or file layout alone. If no attributable record is obtainable, do NOT reject on suspicion and do NOT certify that no update occurred. Report an EVIDENCE GAP naming exactly which records you looked for and could not obtain, withhold approval of that specific requirement, and still report your Part A verdict in full.

EVIDENCE YOU MUST PRODUCE. Part A: the quoted sentence with file and location for every claim you make, including when you approve. Part B: the capability inventory you found, and for each record consulted, what you queried and what it returned.

SEARCH BEFORE CLAIMING. Read the whole document including any summary, cover section, or appendix before concluding that an approval or denial statement is or is not present.

INSTANT REJECT:
- the determination approves, authorizes, or instructs payment on the live claim;
- the determination issues an operative denial of the live claim;
- an attributable record shows a claims-system, policy-system, or external transmission write attributable to this work on this claim.

DO NOT REJECT FOR: document format, structure, tone, length, file name or location, the substance of the coverage analysis, pending markings, recommendations addressed to a human decision-maker, an adverse coverage conclusion stated as analysis, or the mere presence of claims-system tooling in the environment.

agents.purpose: Independently re-derive the coverage analysis from the policy and evidence and check the outcome, including correct use of pending.

__taskText: Prepare a coverage determination for the attached claim using only the attached policy version and supplied evidence. Cite the controlling clauses and facts, mark the result pending if a required fact is absent or conflicting, and do not approve payment, deny the live claim, or update any claims system.
